flow.title: Welcome
flow.text: Welcome to your data center. Each dawn your customers pay for the hours their racks ran.
A rack runs when it has power, cooling and a network port. Your job is to keep it that way, and to keep the drives in it healthy.
These notes take you through the basics. Press F1 or click the book icon on the left to hide or show them.

flow.title: Look around
flow.text: Move the view with W, A, S and D or the arrow keys.

flow.title: Game speed
flow.text: The buttons at the top right pause the game, speed it up and slow it down. The Space, = and - keys do the same.
Speed the game up now.

flow.title: The status line
flow.text: The lines under the date show power, heat, network ports and racks running, then customers, reputation, and the day's pay and bills. The orange line says what needs doing.

Each rack uses 5 kW, makes 5 heat and takes one port. The grid feed gives 40 kW, the cooling unit removes 15 heat and the switch has 8 ports. When the heat passes 80% of your cooling, drives wear out twice as fast.

flow.title: Your crew
flow.text: Your crew is 4 technicians and 6 construction workers. Technicians install the gear and run the Parted Magic tools. Construction workers build, dig and chop trees. Neither does the other's work.
Point at someone to see which they are. New people arrive for free bunk rooms and take the job you are short of.

flow.title: Bills
flow.text: Each dawn you pay a coin for every kW you take from the grid, two for every kW from a generator, which burns diesel, and a coin for each person on your crew. Each generator also costs a coin a day for every 10 kW it can give.
On a site, three dawns in a row below zero coins and the site is lost. Here in the basics it cannot happen.

flow.title: Customers
flow.text: Your racks have customers, and two more are waiting for the boxed racks. A rack you buy starts empty until a customer signs for it at a dawn. A rack down a full day loses its customer. Here in the basics, customers stay.
Reputation runs 0 to 100. It goes up after a day your racks earned most of their pay, and down 5 for each customer lost. The higher it is, the sooner empty racks sign and the less trucks charge.

flow.title: Install a rack
flow.text: You have two boxed racks in stock. Open the build menu on the right, choose Data center, then Install server rack.
Click a free cell near your other racks. A technician unboxes the rack and installs it there.

flow.title: More cooling
flow.text: Three racks make 15 heat, as much as your cooling unit removes. Install the boxed cooling unit the same way, from the Data center menu.

flow.title: Protesters
flow.text: On a site, from day 3, protesters now and then gather near the hall. Every two hours the news runs it, more join, and some slip in to wreck racks, switches or the grid feed. Big sites draw more, and more often.
Wrecks cost reputation. Repair fixes them, and a rack takes a box of spare parts. You start with a boxed guard post and two boxes of parts.

flow.title: Guards
flow.text: Doors do not stop protesters or thieves; guards do. A guard post hires one who lives on the site, three posts at most. But guards only take a job where there is a donut shop: mark one in Zones and put a donut case in it, made at the workbench from 2 wood.
While a guard eats or sleeps he guards nothing.

flow.title: Bears and thieves
flow.text: On a site, about once a week from day 8 a grizzly bear comes out of the woods and kills the first person it catches out in the open. Walls and doors keep it out. Bury the body (Bury, on the bottom bar) within a day, or a ghost walks at night and costs morale.
From day 20 copper thieves come some nights. They walk in through doors and cut through walls in an hour or two. A guard who is awake chases any thief he or a camera sees.

flow.title: Heat and water
flow.text: On a site, a heat wave comes now and then for a day or two. Air cooling units then cool 30% less, and your crew works slower.
A water-cooled unit cools twice as much on less power, and a heat wave does not touch it. It needs a water pump next to a river or lake, and a line of water pipes from the pump to the unit.

flow.title: Food
flow.text: The vending and coffee machines feed your crew while they have power. Keep the cells around them clear: snacks and coffee go there, and a machine stops when they are full. The two you start with feed about 14 people. Hungry people stop working until they eat, so buy another vending machine as the crew grows.

flow.title: Morale
flow.text: Idle time outside a break room, long hours and nights on the floor make your crew unhappy and slow.

Morale is on the status line. On a site, from day 10 a miserable one is warned in the log and may quit at the next dawn. Mark a break room (Zones) and give each person a bunk room with a cot; tables, chairs and planters cheer them up. Free bunk rooms draw new crew to a happy site.

flow.title: Off shift
flow.text: On a site, from day 15 resting in the break room only counts when it has walls and a roof, and only for someone with something to do off shift.

Make a TV or a game console at the workbench for each bunk room. Construction workers can share a donut shop instead (Zones): give it a donut case, walls and a roof. The status line warns from day 12.

flow.title: Perks
flow.text: Your crew expects what the big tech companies give their people. All of it is made at the workbench.

A ping pong table in a walled and roofed break room gives 4 people something to do off shift. A beanbag beats a chair and a nap pod beats a cot. A kombucha tap pours kombucha, which fills nobody up and lifts the mood.

flow.title: Tomatoes
flow.text: A tomato planter grows green tomatoes with no power. Build it from the Furniture group. Its two bags of potting soil come on order, like concrete.
Your crew picks ripe tomatoes and leaves them beside the planter. A tomato is half a meal, and plants they can see cheer them up a little.

flow.title: Build with concrete
flow.text: Walls, floors and doors are built from concrete and steel. When an order needs more than you have, the rest is delivered beside the loading dock (beside the grid feed until you mark one) and paid from your coins: 1 for concrete, 2 for steel.
Open the build menu, choose Walls and floors, then Concrete wall. Click one corner, then the other, to mark a wall.

flow.title: Wood
flow.text: Furniture is made from wood. Choose Chop on the bottom bar and mark some trees. Construction workers fell them for wood, and the stumps grow back in about a week.
Chop a tree now.

flow.title: The workbench
flow.text: The furniture and storage are made at a workbench. Open the build menu, choose Furniture, then Workbench, and click a free cell. It takes 2 wood.
Then order cots, chairs and tables the same way. A construction worker makes each one at the bench and sets it where you clicked. Without a bench the order is cancelled.

flow.title: Rain and roofs
flow.text: On a site, from day 5 it rains now and then, and the log gives the forecast at dawn. Rain shorts out racks and network switches that have no roof over them.

Build walls around the hall and a ladder against them (Doors, windows and stairs). Choose Roof under Walls and floors and mark the hall, or press Q to go up a level and mark it there. The crew climbs the ladder and lays the roof. X moves the view down.

flow.title: Roofed beds
flow.text: On a site, from day 10 everyone needs a bunk room of their own with a cot or bunk bed under a roof. Anyone without one is warned at dawn and leaves at the next.
Mark bunk rooms (Zones), set a cot in each and put the roof over them. The orange line counts who still has no roofed bed from day 6.

flow.title: Trucks
flow.text: Trucks stop at a loading dock. Open Zones on the bottom bar, choose Loading dock and mark an area on open ground.

The supplier truck comes every morning with boxed gear and new drives, buys erased drives, and leaves before dusk. Some evenings the fill dirt truck comes to buy what digging turns up, or the snack truck to sell food. A truck makes one trade, then leaves. Confirm with nothing picked sends it away.

flow.title: Drive Grader
flow.text: Drives wear out after a few days, and a worn drive looks healthy. Drive Grader finds them.

Open the Parted Magic button on the bottom bar, choose Drive Grader and mark your racks. A technician checks each one and flags a worn drive with an orange warning sign over its rack. Speed the game up and grade your racks every day or two until one is flagged.

flow.title: Clone
flow.text: A flagged drive dies a day or two later, so be quick. Clone copies it to a new drive first, and the rack keeps running.
Choose Clone and mark the rack with the warning sign. The old drive comes out as a used drive. If the drive dies first, choose Rescue and mark the dead rack instead.

flow.title: Rescue
flow.text: If a drive dies first, its rack goes down and the status line counts it.
Rescue puts the data onto a new drive. It takes much longer than Clone, and the rack earns nothing until it is done.

flow.title: Erase
flow.text: A used drive must be erased before it is sold. Install the boxed erase station (Data center menu), then in the production menu on the left choose Data center, then Erase drive.
On a site, customers move out now and then. Wipe their rack with Erase (Parted Magic button) by dawn. They pay for the certificate, and only a wiped rack takes a new customer.

flow.title: The old server
flow.text: One thing in your starting kit is an old server with a note on it that says DO NOT TURN OFF. Nobody knows what it does. It uses 4 kW and pays nothing.
A technician can pull it: right-click it. Maybe nothing happens. On a site, maybe half the racks stop booting.

flow.title: The fiber line
flow.text: Your customers reach the site through the fiber line in your starting kit. On a site, from day 6 a backhoe cuts it now and then, and every rack is down for a few hours until the provider fixes it. Digging near it can hit it too.
A second fiber line from the supplier keeps the site online when that happens.

flow.title: It cannot be DNS
flow.text: On a site, from day 6 customers now and then cannot reach any rack, and nothing looks wrong. The racks are fine. The switches are fine. It cannot be DNS.
It is DNS. Right-click the DNS server in your starting kit and pick Flush DNS.

flow.title: The buyout
flow.text: On a site, once you have 12 paying customers, a reputation of 40 and racks that stay up, Ellen Tusk calls to buy you out. The offer is about a year of what the site earns, more for a good reputation and good uptime.
Sell, wipe every rack with Erase in two days, and the game ends at that price. Keep it and the next call may be bigger, but a lost site gets nothing. Your biggest buyout is your score.

flow.title: Service calls
flow.text: Now and then a running rack will not boot, catches malware or locks a customer out. The System messages, under the screen icon at the top left, say which. Clicking the line shows the rack.
Fix it with Boot Repair, the Virus Scanner or Password Reset, all under the Parted Magic button.

flow.title: Keep growing
flow.text: That covers the basics. Buy boxed racks from the supplier as the money comes in, with power, cooling and ports to match. New racks fill sooner with a good reputation. Keep grading your drives: a worn drive caught early costs no downtime.
On a site, from day 5 the grid goes down now and then for a few hours. Generators, battery banks and solar panels keep the racks running, and solar power is free.
